name: GitHub Build Monitor
author: Jankees
description: Whether main is green right now: a mark that spins while a build runs, holds green for a minute after one passes, and stays red until a later build fixes it.

barWidget.description: GitHub Actions on the default branch of one repository, rolled up per commit. The panel lists the last builds with their duration and status, and a click opens one on GitHub.

schema.label: GitHub project
schema.description: Paste the GitHub URL of the project, for example https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy. owner/name works too. Authentication comes from the gh CLI, so private repositories work as long as gh can see them.

schema.label: Branch
schema.description: Leave empty to follow the repository's default branch, whether that is main or master.

schema.label: Bar label
schema.description: Text next to the mark. Empty uses the repository name without its owner.

schema.label: Show the label
schema.description: Off by default: the mark on its own is enough when you track one project. Turn it on when the bar carries more than one.

schema.label: Flag paths containing
schema.description: Comma separated. A build whose commit touched a file with one of these in its path gets a mark in the list. Empty turns it off, which also saves an API call per new commit.

schema.label: Hold green for (seconds)
schema.description: How long a passing build stays green in the bar before the mark steps back to neutral. A failed build has no timer and stays red.
